title: Shadows & Sundials
strapline: Chase your shadow, freeze it in chalk, and watch it slide round as the sun crosses the sky.
intent: Children explore light and shadow, discovering that a shadow needs light and something to block it.
Children observe change over time — shadows move, shrink and stretch as the day goes on.
Children investigate cause and effect: move the object, move the light, and the shadow changes.
Children use comparative and positional language — longer, shorter, behind, in front.
Children ask real questions about the sun, light and why shadows behave as they do.
implementation: On a sunny day, go shadow-hunting outside — chase them, hide them, make them touch, make them huge.
Draw round a child's shadow in chalk in the morning, then come back at lunch to see it has moved.
Set up a torch and screen inside so children can make and change shadows on demand.
Ask what makes a shadow bigger, smaller or disappear, and let children test their ideas.
Make a simple sundial — a stick in the ground, chalk marks through the day — and watch time move.
Feed in the language of comparison and position as shadows stretch and shrink.
Follow children's big questions about the sun and light, looking things up together.
key_questions: What do you need to make a shadow?
Why do you think your shadow moved since this morning?
How could you make your shadow bigger — or smaller?
What happens to the shadow when we move the torch?
Where will the shadow be after lunch, do you think?

impact.text: Children explore light and shadow and discover a shadow needs light and something to block it.
Children observe change over time as shadows move, shrink and stretch through the day.
Children investigate cause and effect — move the object or light, change the shadow.
Children use comparative and positional language — longer, shorter, behind, in front.
Children ask real questions about the sun and light and predict what will happen.
Children stay with the investigation, testing idea after idea to change the shadow.

enhancements: Chalk for drawing round shadows through the day.
Torches, lamps and a white screen or sheet for indoor shadows.
A stick sundial and chalk marks to track the sun.
Shadow puppets and figures to project and animate.
Transparent, translucent and opaque materials to test what casts a shadow.
A camera to record the shadow's changing position.
Books about the sun, light and shadows to follow children's questions.

playing_exploring: Children play with their own shadows, chasing, hiding and stretching them.
They explore the torch and screen freely to see what shadows they can make.
active_learning: Children return through the day to check how the shadow has moved.
They test idea after idea to make a shadow grow, shrink or vanish.
creating_thinking: Children predict where a shadow will fall and what will change it.
They form theories about light and the sun and test them out.
